Rich text with zero dependencies.

A WYSIWYG editor in plain JavaScript. No jQuery, no runtime packages, no execCommand: every command is the editor's own DOM transform, so Chrome, Firefox and Safari produce the same markup.

$ npm install autumnnote-plus

What's in it

Everything a writer reaches for, in one script.

Each feature is its own module, started only when its option is on. Turn off what you do not use, or load the core build and add your own.

  1. +01

    Writing

    A bubble toolbar on selection, Markdown shortcuts as you type, a slash command menu, @mentions, checklists and floating find & replace.

  2. +02

    Images and video

    Drag-and-drop upload, resize handles and a crop overlay for images; YouTube and Vimeo embeds that resize the same way. An emoji picker with about 380 emoji.

  3. +03

    Tables

    Insert from a size grid, merge and split cells, shade them, add a header row, and edit rows and columns from a tooltip that sits on the table.

  4. +04

    Code

    Code blocks with Prism highlighting and language detection, inline code, and a source view for editing the HTML directly.

  5. +05

    Clean output

    HTML or Markdown in and out with getHTML() and getMarkdown(). Paste and drop go through a DOM sanitiser. Character and word limits, and autosave with restore.

  6. +06

    Fits your app

    Light, dark or automatic theme, design tokens through themeVars, your own keyboard map and buttons, a plugin API, right-to-left text and nine interface languages.

Why this fork

          
The same editor, with the holes closed.

          
autumnnote-plus starts from Autumn Note 3.1.0 by Minh Pham. A security audit of that release found ways for sanitised content to turn back into live markup. Each one is fixed here with a regression test, and each was reported to the original maintainer.

          

            Read the 4.0.0 changelog
            Security policy
          

        


        
    
          
  • 
            
    Undo and redo
    
            
    History snapshots used a predictable token for image data, so an author could type it into an attribute and get an event handler back on undo. Tokens are now random per editor.
    
          
    • 
          
  • 
            
    getHTML() and print
    
            
    String cleanup after serialising could complete a --> or </xmp> terminator. Cleanup now runs on a cloned DOM, and raw-text elements are removed.
    
          
    • 
          
  • 
            
    Drag and drop
    
            
    HTML dragged in from another page skipped the sanitiser. It is now cleaned like a paste; drags inside the editor stay native moves.
    
          
    • 
          
  • 
            
    Mentions and names
    
            
    The default mention chip inserted its label as HTML, and name attributes could shadow document members. Labels are text now and name is removed.
    
          
    • 
          
  • 
            
    Markdown and slow input
    
            
    Markdown export keeps inert text inert for the next renderer, and the parsers that took seconds on crafted input run in linear time.
    
          
    • 
        

      

    


    
    

      

        

          

            
Install

            
Pick your setup.

          

          

            
            
            
            
          

        


        

          

            
            
            
            
          


          

            

              $
              npm install autumnnote-plus
              
            

            

              
              
import AutumnNote from 'autumnnote-plus';
import 'autumnnote-plus/dist/autumnnote.css';

const editor = AutumnNote.create('#editor', {
  placeholder: 'Start typing…',
  bubbleToolbar: true,
  onChange(html) { save(html); },
});

            

          


          

            

              $
              npm install autumnnote-plus autumnnote-plus-react
              
            

            

              
              
import { useRef } from 'react';
import AutumnNoteEditor from 'autumnnote-plus-react';
import 'autumnnote-plus/dist/autumnnote.css';

export function Editor() {
  const ref = useRef(null);
  return <AutumnNoteEditor ref={ref} options={{ placeholder: 'Start typing…' }} />;
}

No build step. The script registers a global AutumnNote; for a language other than English, add its locale script after it.

            

              
              
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/autumnnote-plus/dist/autumnnote.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/autumnnote-plus"></script>
<!-- optional: one locale -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/autumnnote-plus/dist/i18n/id.umd.js"></script>
<script>
  AutumnNote.create('#editor', { lang: 'id' });
</script>

            

          

        

      

    


    
    

      

        

          
Questions

          
Before you switch.

        

        

          

            How is autumnnote-plus different from autumnnote?
            
It is an unofficial fork of Autumn Note 3.1.0. The API, options, events, CSS classes and the AutumnNote global are unchanged. On top of that come the security fixes above, an Indonesian locale, keyboard and contrast fixes in the editor UI, and a CDN build that no longer carries every language (109 KB down to 93 KB gzip).

          

          

            Can I switch without changing my imports?
            
Yes. Install it under the old name with an npm alias: npm install autumnnote@npm:autumnnote-plus@^4.0.0. Code that imports 'autumnnote' keeps working.

          

          

            Is it free to use?
            
Yes. It is MIT licensed, like the original project, for personal and commercial use.

          

          

            Which package managers and Node.js versions work?
            
npm, pnpm, yarn and Bun all install it; pick yours in the switch above the install command. The package asks for Node 22.22.2 or newer, or 24.15.0 or newer. The CDN build needs only a modern browser.

          

          

            Does it use document.execCommand?
            
No. Every formatting command is the editor's own DOM transform, tested in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Copy and cut use the async Clipboard API.
